inputs.share_count_basis: 620,435,200 shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (Interim Report 2026, after the 31.0m-share January 2026 top-up subscription). 23.64m share options at HK$39.60 are out of the money at the current price and anti-dilutive (diluted EPS count 615.886m is a weighted average, not the closing count). Count held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution too would double-count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash flow statement, 'Equity-settled share-based payment expenses' US$5,195k (2610.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:7323); no equity-award cash taxes (options unvested, none exercised). H1 FY2026 charge US$5,865k is the first full half of the July-2025 grant.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows in USD; HKEX quote in HKD. USD->HKD 7.8463 from Yahoo USDHKD=X on 2026-10-22 (HKD peg band 7.75-7.85). No dual listing to parity-check; the January 2026 placing at HK$64.50 = US$8.26/share and the option exercise price HK$39.60 = US$5.05 both tie to ~7.84, which confirms the direction. Per-share values are computed in USD and multiplied by fx_rate to HKD.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-22T02:25:00Z (HKEX regular session, intraday 10:25 HKT; 52-week range 21.96-74.80, price is within 1.4% of the 52-week low)
inputs.net_cash_note: Cash and cash equivalents US$666.746m at 30 June 2026 (Interim Report 2026 note 12), which already includes the ~US$255m net placing proceeds received 30 January 2026 (~90% earmarked for the Electrolytic Aluminium Project) and the ~US$85m unutilised IPO proceeds. That earmarked cash is added in the bridge and the project spend it funds is deducted through the capex path, so it is counted once. Time deposits (US$0.442m) and restricted deposits (US$0.730m) are left out of net cash. No bank borrowings; lease liabilities US$0.011m.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, so a USD-built rate: 10-year UST ~4.2% + beta 1.2 x 5.0% ERP = 10.2%, plus ~1pp Indonesia single-site country/operational premium = ~11%. No debt, so WACC = cost of equity. Held at 11% in all three scenarios; the alumina price cycle, bauxite-quota risk and smelter execution are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) leases as debt: lease liabilities (US$0.011m) sit in total_debt, lease principal (US$68k/half) is not deducted from the flows. Immaterial either way.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (NCI share of profit was 2.3% of FY2025 net income, US$1.6m in H1 FY2026). NCI deducted once, at book value US$34.74m (30 June 2026), via equity_bridge. Press Metal's historic BAI minority was swapped into the listco pre-IPO; the residual NCI is small.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF with mid-cycle normalisation (dcf-methods routing: operating company, non-US, cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). First valuation of this ticker. Pure-play alumina refiner: revenue = volume x index-linked ASP, so the driver paths are built from volume x ASP x unit cost, not from historical CAGRs (only 2.5 years of listed history, all of them a price cycle: ASP US$473/t FY2024 -> 432 FY2025 -> 320 H1 FY2026; 10-year Platts alumina average ~US$360-370/t). EBITDA margin paths are ex-interest income (the CSV EBITDA = PBT + D&A and so includes US$13.2m FY2025 interest income; that income is stripped because the US$667m cash pile is added in the bridge). Cash tax: BAI holds a 20-year Indonesian CIT exemption (2021-2040) on the first 2Mt and has Ministry of Finance prior consent for the same on the new 2Mt, but OECD Pillar Two (15% minimum, in force in Indonesia/HK/Singapore from 2025) added US$50.2m to FY2025 tax; FY2025 book ETR 12.8%, cash tax 6% of PBT. Paths ramp to the 15% Pillar Two floor net of substance carve-outs. Terminal cap multiple 12x (cyclical). Horizon 10 years because the smelter changes the revenue/margin mix through FY2030.

equity_bridge.note: Interim Report 2026 balance sheet, 30 June 2026; flows are consolidated so NCI is deducted once here

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: terminal nominal growth for a mid-cycle commodity producer; history is too short (FY2023-FY2025 only) and spans one price cycle plus a capacity doubling, so no CAGR is a usable forward rate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 2-yr CAGR 42.4% vs revenue 29.8% vs EPS 43.4% all reflect the 2Mt->4Mt capacity doubling, the March 2025 IPO (US$298m) and the FY2024 alumina price peak; none is repeatable. Owner FCF went 15 -> 300 -> -51 (capex). Forward growth is built bottom-up from volume x ASP.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026: 2.75Mt x ~US$335/t (H1 actual 1.296Mt @ 320; H2 ~1.45Mt @ ~350 after the August rebound to 348) = ~US$923m, -19%. FY2027: 3.3Mt @ 355 as RKAB bauxite constraints ease. FY2028: 3.7Mt @ 370 (mid-cycle = 10-yr Platts average). FY2029: external alumina 3.5Mt (0.4Mt consumed internally) + 250kt smelter phase 1 commissioning (200kt sold @ ~US$2,500/t) = ~US$1.8bn, +31%. FY2030: full 250kt, ~US$1.9bn. FY2031+: 2.5% nominal price drift; the 500kt phase 2 is unfunded and undated so it is bull-only.
base.margin_rationale: Ex-interest EBITDA/t: cash cost ~US$235/t (H1 FY2026 cost of sales US$270/t incl. ~US$34/t depreciation) + ~US$9/t SG&A. At ASP 335 -> 27%; 355 -> 31%; 370 at 3.7Mt -> 34%. From FY2029 the smelter dilutes the blended margin (metal revenue at ~US$250/t conversion EBITDA on ~US$2,500/t price) to ~29.5%, drifting to 29% for cost inflation.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 ~US$250m (US$203m PPE payables at Dec-25 unwinding plus smelter preparatory spend; H1 actual 116.7). FY2027 ~US$220m and FY2028 ~US$150m complete the US$436.6m phase-1 smelter. Thereafter 5% of revenue sustaining (~US$95m on US$1.9bn, roughly 0.8x D&A on long-life plant).
base.tax_rationale: Pillar Two 15% floor net of substance-based carve-outs (tangible-asset carve-out large on ~US$1.5bn PP&E, transitional rates declining to 5% by 2033) plus dividend WHT. FY2025 book ETR 12.8%; ramps 12% -> 15% as carve-outs shrink. The first-2Mt CIT exemption runs to 2040, outside the explicit horizon, so the terminal rate is the Pillar Two floor.

bull.growth_rationale: ASP recovers to US$370 in H2 FY2026 and a US$410/t mid-cycle (Indonesian refinery pipeline slips, Chinese bauxite costs stay high); volume reaches 4.0Mt by FY2027; smelter phase 1 on time in FY2029 at US$2,600/t aluminium; the 500kt phase 2 is self-funded from FY2030-FY2032 (capex 12-14% of revenue) and ships from FY2032-FY2033.
bull.margin_rationale: ASP 410 at cash cost 230 -> 38% peak-ish alumina margin in FY2028; smelter mix dilutes to 32-33%.

bear.growth_rationale: Global alumina surplus persists as the Indonesian pipeline (~30Mt) and Chinese additions land: ASP stuck at US$310-320/t, near Chinese marginal cost. RKAB bauxite quotas cap volume at ~3.0-3.2Mt and lift cash cost to ~US$245/t. Smelter slips a year (first metal FY2029, 150kt) into a US$2,300/t aluminium market. No phase 2.
bear.margin_rationale: EBITDA/t ~US$55 (315 - 245 - 10 SG&A) -> ~18%; FY2026 22% on the H1 actual plus a weaker H2.
bear.tax_rationale: New-project CIT exemption not finally approved: 22% Indonesian CIT on half the output blends with Pillar Two to ~18%.

scenario_narratives.base: Alumina troughs in 2026 (company ASP ~US$335/t for the year) and reverts to a ~US$365-370/t mid-cycle by 2028 as new electrolytic capacity outside China absorbs the Indonesian and Chinese refinery additions. The 4Mt plant runs at 3.3Mt in 2027 and 3.7Mt from 2028 once RKAB bauxite approvals normalise; cash cost holds ~US$235/t. The US$436.6m 250kt smelter is built 2026-2028 from the placing proceeds and cash on hand, commissions in 2029 and earns a modest ~US$250/t conversion margin, lifting revenue to ~US$1.9bn but diluting the blended EBITDA margin to ~29.5%. Phase 2 (500kt) is not in the base. Pillar Two sets a 15% cash-tax floor by 2030.
scenario_narratives.bull: Alumina rebounds faster (US$410/t mid-cycle) because the Indonesian refinery pipeline slips and Chinese refiners stay cost-constrained by imported bauxite; the plant reaches 4Mt in 2027 at a 38% margin. The smelter is on time and on budget, aluminium holds ~US$2,600/t under China's capacity cap, and management self-funds the 500kt phase 2 from 2030, shipping in 2032-2033. Terminal cap 14x.
scenario_narratives.bear: Oversupply is structural: ASP sits at US$310-320/t for years, bauxite quotas cap output near 3Mt and push cash cost toward US$245/t, so EBITDA/t collapses to ~US$55. The smelter is late and commissions into a soft metal market; the new-project tax exemption is not finalised and Pillar Two plus Indonesian CIT take ~18%. Dividends track the trough. The net cash pile and the plant's replacement value are most of what is left; terminal cap 10x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% house default: pure index-priced commodity with no hedging, single site, bauxite supply under a government quota that already bit in H1 FY2026, related-party control (combined Chairman/CEO, Nanshan Group as parent and supplier, Press Metal as shareholder-customer) and 2.5 years of listed history. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things at once: an ASP recovery to US$410, on-time smelter execution in a new business line, and a self-funded phase 2. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A low-cost, debt-free, 4Mt single-site alumina refiner valued on mid-cycle owner FCF rather than on either the FY2024 peak (55% EBITDA margin) or the H1 FY2026 trough (26%). Net cash of US$667m is ~38% of the market capitalisation at the current price, so the market is paying ~US$1.1bn of enterprise value for a plant that cost more than that to build and that earns US$450-500m of EBITDA at a US$370/t alumina price. The value hinges on where alumina settles once the current Indonesian/Chinese capacity wave is absorbed, and on whether the smelter earns its cost of capital.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle ASP assumption (US$365-370/t): each US$10/t is ~US$37m of EBITDA at 3.7Mt, roughly HK$2.5/share of value
Bauxite availability and cost under Indonesia's RKAB quota system; the plant cannot run at 4Mt without it
Smelter phase 1 execution (US$436.6m, new power-intensive business) and the aluminium price at commissioning
Pillar Two / CIT exemption outcome: 15% vs ~18-22% effective cash tax
Single-site operational risk (Bintan) and related-party governance; dividend policy tracks profit so there is no payout floor
Cash pile is partly earmarked for the smelter: it is in the bridge once and the spend is in the capex path, but a phase-2 commitment would re-direct it

sanity_check_review.trip_reason_reported: Base case upside 124% with price in the upper half of the 10yr range (359%); diagnosis wacc_too_low (regulatory single point of failure)
sanity_check_review.assessment: False trip from the known sanity_check fx-direction bug (USD filer / HKD quote): the historical table multiplies the HK$64.70 FY2025 year-end price by 7.8463 instead of dividing, giving P/B 154x, EV/EBITDA 531x, P/S 252x and a 'price position' of 359% of the range. On a consistent USD basis the FY2025 year-end market paid P/E 11.9x, P/B 2.6x, EV/EBITDA 8.4x, P/S 4.3x; the current price (HK$22.24 = US$2.83) is at 0.5% of its 52-week range and trades at P/E 4.3x FY2025, P/B 0.86x, EV/EBITDA 2.1x trailing / 2.4x mid-cycle. The implied multiples the check printed (P/E 70x, EV/EBITDA 52x) divide an HKD value by USD per-share metrics.
sanity_check_review.fix_rationale: No model fix is warranted: the base IV implies 6.1x trailing / 7.1x mid-cycle EV/EBITDA and 1.9x book, below what the market paid at FY2025 year-end (8.4x, 2.6x), so the model is not assuming a re-rating. The single-site/regulatory risk the diagnosis names is already charged once: ~1pp Indonesia premium inside the 11% USD WACC plus a 30% bear weight on a bear case (HK$18.52) that sits below the current price. Stacking a further WACC premium on top of the probability-weighted scenarios would charge the same risk twice (owner-fcf-adaptations section f).

implied_multiples_after_fix.basis: USD, SBC-adjusted; FY2025 EPS 0.72, H1 FY2026 book US$2,053.5m, FY2025 EBITDA ex-SBC US$541.3m, mid-cycle FY2028 EBITDA ~US$466m, EV = equity - net cash + NCI
